Section 4.3: Financial Transaction Records
All transactional metadata, including client identifiers, amount fields, and timestamped settlement data, shall be retained for a mandatory period of seven (7) years from the date of the transaction to satisfy local tax and anti-money laundering (AML) regulatory requirements.

Section 5.1: Right to Erasure (GDPR/CCPA Compliance)
Upon receipt of a verified 'Request for Deletion' (RfD), the Data Privacy Office (DPO) shall facilitate the removal of all personally identifiable information (PII) from active production databases. The client (Meridian) is pushing back on our standard DPA template. They are claiming our current sub-processor notification period is insufficient for their compliance audit requirements. ---
[ATTACHED DOCUMENT: MERIDIAN_LOGISTICS_DPA_REDLINE_V2.docx]

Clause 12.4: Data Breach Notification
In the event of a confirmed Personal Data Breach, Processor shall notify Controller without undue delay, and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of such breach. Processor shall provide a written report describing the nature of the breach, the categories of data affected, and the remediation steps taken.

Clause 14.1: Sub-processor Engagement
Processor may engage sub-processors to assist in the performance of its obligations under this Agreement. Processor shall maintain an up-to-date list of sub-processors on its website. Processor shall notify Controller of any intended changes concerning the addition or replacement of sub-processors at least thirty (30) days prior to such change taking effect. Controller shall have the right to object to such changes on reasonable grounds related to data protection.

[REPLY FROM CLIENT DPO - MARCUS THORNE]
"Regarding the DPA version 2.0 draft, we find the notification window in Clause 14.1 to be a significant gap in our risk management framework. Under our current internal governance protocols for 2025, any change in the processing chain requires a minimum of sixty (60) calendar days for our security team to conduct a secondary impact assessment. Please amend Clause 14.1 to reflect a 60-day notice period. Additionally, we noticed that your standard template does not explicitly mention the 'right to audit' in the context of sub-processor security, though we recognize this may be covered under the general audit provisions in Section 9."
